ESOSUKSince 2014

ESOS

Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme

The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme makes large UK organisations audit their energy use every four years and find ways to save. Since Phase 3 you must also publish an action plan and report progress against it every year. Phase 4 runs to 5 December 2027.

Draft guide. We're checking this page against official sources before launch. Always confirm with your regulator.

Step 1

Are you in scope?

You're probably in if…

  • Your UK group has 250 or more employees, or
  • Turnover above £44 million and balance sheet above £38 million
  • Size is measured across your whole UK corporate group on the qualification date (31 December 2026 for Phase 4)

You're probably out if…

  • Small and medium-sized groups below both thresholds
  • Public bodies, with some exceptions

Who regulates it: Environment Agency (UK scheme administrator), with SEPA, Natural Resources Wales and NIEA. Submissions go through the MESOS reporting system.

Step 2

Your yearly routine

  1. Qualification dateCheck whether your group is large on 31 December 2026
  2. Before compliance dateMeasure energy use, audit it, get lead assessor and board sign-off
  3. 5 Dec 2027Notify compliance and submit your action plan
  4. Each 5 Dec afterReport progress against your action plan

Key facts

Penalties
No audit: up to £50,000, plus up to £500 per working day for up to 80 working days. Failing to notify: up to £5,000
Sign-off
Board-level directors and an approved lead assessor
Phase 4 thresholds
Unchanged from Phase 3
Overlap
Many ESOS companies also report under SECR
Practical tip

Reuse your SECR energy data for ESOS. It saves weeks, but check the coverage periods line up.
